transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-05
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood CSM), Evan Chu (Redwood SE), Laura Kim (Oceanview Head of Data), Marcus Allen (VP Eng), Priya Singh (Security), Diego Ramos (PM)

Summary (auto): Kickoff went through onboarding milestones, security requirements, initial pilot scope, and scheduling for a benchmark cluster. Customer emphasized SSO, encryption, and data residency concerns. Redwood outlined Dedicated vs Hosted options and suggested next steps.

Transcript:
[00:00:08] Jordan Blake: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Uh, this is Jordan from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. With me today is Samira, our CSM, and Evan, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?

[00:00:18] Laura Kim: Hi Jordan, thanks, doing good. Marcus and Priya and Diego are here as well. Excited to kick this off.

[00:00:28] Marcus Allen: Yep, morning/afternoon. We wanted to cover timeline, security, and, um, what the pilot looks like.

[00:00:40] Samira Patel: Great. We'll run through the onboarding plan and then Evan can go into the technical checklist and benchmark idea.

[00:00:50] Evan Chu: Cool. Quick note, if anyone's looking at Dedicated versus Hosted, we typically start Hosted for quick time-to-value then move to Dedicated once throughput/latency needs and data isolation are settled. But we can also pilot Dedicated if you prefer.

[00:01:05] Priya Singh: From security perspective, we need SOC2, SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and support for customer-managed keys (KMS / HSM). Also data residency - all PHI stays in our VPC.

[00:01:22] Jordan Blake: Totally, we've done that before. We'll share our SOC2 report and a security pack. We support SSO via SAML, SCIM for users, and KMS integrations — we can outline the KMS flow in the packet.

[00:01:35] Diego Ramos: How does Redwood handle key management for private deployments vs hosted?

[00:01:44] Evan Chu: For Hosted, we encrypt at rest and we do not manage customer KMS unless requested; for Private/Dedicated we can support customer-managed KMS/HSM in the VPC. There can be an on-prem option if needed. There was a small audio glitch here.

[00:02:05] Laura Kim: Ok can you also confirm audit logs and retention? We need to surface who called what model, per-team usage.

[00:02:13] Samira Patel: Yes, audit logs are available in Redwood Console; we can turn on token-level tracing and long-term retention is an add-on. We'll include the logging retention options in the security pack.

[00:02:30] Marcus Allen: On performance — our main concern is latency for interactive clinical assistant features. We expect p95 under 400ms ideally, with bursts up to 200 QPS. Cost is a factor too.

[00:02:45] Evan Chu: Right — there's always a tradeoff. We can look at model variants and quantization; for low-latency interactive we recommend smaller tuned model or a GPU-backed Dedicated pool with optimized kernels and KV cache pinned. We'll propose a benchmark plan.

[00:03:05] Priya Singh: For networking, we need VPC peering or private link and firewall rules. Also, can you support static egress IPs?

[00:03:16] Evan Chu: Yes, static egress IPs are possible for Dedicated/private setups. We'll include a networking checklist: CIDR ranges, ports, peering, and NAT requirements.

[00:03:32] Diego Ramos: What's the usual timeline for onboarding to production?

[00:03:38] Jordan Blake: Typically 4-8 weeks: week 1-2 setup and security validation, week 2-4 pilot/benchmarks, week 4-6 rollouts and production cutover depending on your internal approvals. We'll tailor this to Oceanview's timeline.

[00:03:55] Laura Kim: We have a compliance review the week of April 19th, so it'd be great to have the security docs before then.

[00:04:05] Samira Patel: We'll aim to get SOC2 and the security packet to you by April 6th.

[00:04:12] Marcus Allen: For the bench, we'd like Redwood to run a short test with a sample prompt set (clinical summarization, note completion) and provide latency and cost estimates.

[00:04:24] Evan Chu: Perfect. We'll need sample payload sizes, concurrency targets, and a small prompt corpus — if you can provide that we'll schedule the benchmark on a Dedicated test pool or hosted with traffic shaping.

[00:04:40] Laura Kim: We can share a sample of 500 prompts and expected QPS distribution by Friday.

[00:04:47] Marcus Allen: One more question — how do rollouts and canaries work? We want model pinning during pilot and gradual rollout.

[00:04:56] Evan Chu: Redwood supports model pinning and rollouts via the Console: canary percentages, automatic fallback to previous model if error/latency breaches, and route-based policies. We'll demo that during the technical deep dive.

[00:05:10] Diego Ramos: Any compliance red flags around PHI?

[00:05:15] Samira Patel: We have customers handling PHI on Redwood Private with customer-managed keys and VPC isolation. For hosted we offer contractual terms and data controls, but some customers prefer Dedicated/private for strict PHI rules.

[00:05:28] Priya Singh: Ok that's helpful. Also, need to confirm retention windows and deletion procedures for cached prompts/kv.

[00:05:36] Evan Chu: We'll include explicit cache retention controls in the documentation and options to disable caching for sensitive workloads during pilot.

[00:05:50] Jordan Blake: Logistics — I'll send the onboarding deck and quickstart checklist. Samira will send the security pack. Evan will follow up on the benchmark plan and resource ask. Marcus/Laura will provide the prompt corpus and QPS targets.

[00:06:05] Marcus Allen: Sounds good. Who is the primary contact for the technical deep dive?

[00:06:10] Priya Singh: That will be me for security and Marcus for infra; Diego will coordinate product questions.

[00:06:20] Evan Chu: I'll coordinate the technical deep dive — propose week of April 12th. We'll cover VPC peering, IAM, static egress, KMS flow, and the bench plan.

[00:06:30] Laura Kim: Week of April 12th works for us.

[00:06:36] Jordan Blake: Great. Any other blockers we didn't surface?

[00:06:40] Diego Ramos: Only approvals internally — procurement will need pricing, and security needs the SOC2 doc.

[00:06:47] Samira Patel: We'll include a pricing estimate for the pilot in the follow-up and an outline of Dedicated vs Hosted cost drivers.

[00:06:58] Marcus Allen: Are there any required contracts to start a pilot?

[00:07:03] Jordan Blake: For most pilots we have a short pilot agreement; for Dedicated there's usually a reserved capacity contract but we can do a limited short-term trial to gather bench data. Legal can share a pilot SOW template.

[00:07:15] Laura Kim: Ok thanks. Also curious about tooling — can we get token-level cost breakdown per team?

[00:07:22] Samira Patel: Yes, Console has per-route and per-model token/cost breakdowns, and we can set up alerts for regression on eval prompts.

[00:07:32] Diego Ramos: Mention any competitors? We evaluated Anthropic and Bedrock; cost/latency was a big part of the evaluation.

[00:07:40] Jordan Blake: Understood — we often benchmark against those. We'll include a short comparison matrix in the follow-up.

[00:07:48] Marcus Allen: If we go Dedicated, how long to scale up capacity?

[00:07:53] Evan Chu: With Reserved capacity planning typically 2-4 weeks for provisioning depending on region and hardware, but we can do burst/beta capacity while reserved infra comes up.

[00:08:05] Priya Singh: Anything on data residency for EU customers later?

[00:08:10] Jordan Blake: We have region options and can scope private deployments in-region; we'll add that to the doc.

[00:08:18] --- [discussion continues; mid call notes, some crosstalk and short pauses] ---

[00:20:15] Evan Chu: Quick technical note on KV cache: for summarization workloads keeping prefix cache across requests can dramatically cut token cost and latency, but for PHI you might want to disable or limit caching.

[00:21:02] Priya Singh: That's critical — we'd likely want caching off or highly controlled for PHI. Any support for encryption-in-flight on cached KVs?

[00:21:15] Evan Chu: Yes, KV encryption-in-flight and at-rest can be configured; we'll surface the exact options in the security packet.

[00:28:47] Jordan Blake: We're going to propose the following milestones: 1) Share docs and security pack (Apr 6), 2) Technical deep dive (week of Apr 12), 3) Benchmarks/pilot (Apr 12-16), 4) Review results and next steps (Apr 19-23).

[00:29:05] Laura Kim: That fits our compliance calendar.

[00:29:12] Diego Ramos: On pricing — if pilot shows we need Dedicated, what's the commitment look like?

[00:29:20] Samira Patel: Dedicated is typically reserved monthly/annual commits. For pilots we can discuss a short-term reserved window or convert pilot usage into a commitment if both sides agree.

[00:30:03] Marcus Allen: Any specific logs we should expect for auditing?

[00:30:09] Samira Patel: Audit logs include request traces, model version, user identity, and token counts. We can show an example export in the follow-up.

[00:30:28] Evan Chu: For the bench we'll capture p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, token cost, and memory footprints. Also note any model-specific tuning we apply.

[00:31:00] Laura Kim: Ok we'll prepare sample prompts and the QPS distribution by Friday.

[00:31:08] Jordan Blake: Perfect — we'll follow up with the deliverables. Anything else before we wrap?

[00:31:14] Priya Singh: No, just please include corporate legal contacts for pilot agreement.

[00:31:20] Jordan Blake: Will do. Thanks everyone. We'll send the decks and security pack, and Evan will reach out to schedule the technical deep dive.

[00:31:28] Marcus Allen: Thanks all.

[00:31:30] [call ends]

Notes: transcription contains small imperfections and short overlaps; speaker labels are accurate to best-effort.
